section_entries.label: 4. Moments of L-functions in families
section_entries.mathematical_role: Transfers the method to unitary, symplectic, and orthogonal families and isolates the prime-square contribution that shifts the Gaussian center.

unit_result_entry.title: Prime squares shift the center for quadratic Dirichlet L-values
unit_result_entry.why_material: Shows that prime squares are no longer negligible, contribute half a log-log term, and force a shifted large-value threshold before reciprocity and Polya-Vinogradov provide the mean-value analogue.

unit_dependency_entry.context_note: The proof is intentionally sketched; the stated tail and moment bounds are conditional on GRH and the named family-specific averaging tools.
unit_dependency_entry.representation_dependency: Exact shifts and exponents are formula-sensitive; the prime-square cause and shifted threshold are explicit.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Unitary-family transfer replaces time averaging by character orthogonality
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Identifies the sole structural modification for primitive characters: character orthogonality controls the analogue of the off-diagonal terms in the mean-value lemma.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Prime squares shift the center oppositely for elliptic-curve twists
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Repeats the explicit-formula architecture with elliptic-curve coefficients and finds a negative half-log-log prime-square contribution, producing the orthogonal-family moment exponent.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: The same prime-polynomial architecture transfers across families, while the negligible, positive, or negative prime-square term tracks the unitary, symplectic, or orthogonal shift in the expected Gaussian center.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The family arguments are sketches under GRH, exact constants are formula-sensitive, and the stronger Selberg analogues additionally require control of near-central zeros.
related_synthesis_entries.title: Prime-square mass predicts the family-dependent center
